newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power steady to up on weather, gas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power steady to up on weather, gas.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were steady to higher Wednesday, supported by firmer natural gas prices and cooler weather forecasts, market sources said.

Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to remain about 10 to 15 degrees F above normal through early Thursday. Cooler weather is forecast for the region late Thursday and into the weekend as a front moves in from the Midwest.
Firm, peak power prices into Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) for Thursday were in the $16.00-17.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared with Tuesday's trading at $16.00-17.00.

TVA's 1,065 MW Browns Ferry 2 nuclear power unit in Alabama remained at 29 percent of capacity this morning. Unit 3, with an identical generating capacity, was at 82 percent power and coasting down to a refueling outage February 21.
Firm, off-peak power prices into TVA were talked at $13.50-14.00 per MWh.
March TVA prices were talked in the $19.50-20.00 per MWh range, while the April market hovered in the $18.10-18.40 area. May TVA prices were at $18.60-18.90, traders said.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak power prices in 16 hour blocks for Thursday were mostly steady in the $19.50-20.50 per MWh range.
Firm, off-peak power for Thursday at the Ga./Fla. border was still assessed at $14.00 per MWh.
Separately, Florida Power and Light Co's 666 MW Turkey Point 4 returned to full power after operating at 60 percent output Tuesday for cleaning and maintenance.
Duke Power's 846 MW Oconee 2 nuclear unit in South Carolina, shut since last September after a steam pipe burst, also resumed full power operations.
Oconee unit 1 will likely restart this weekend, the company said, while unit 3 is expected to resume power output later this month.
The units have a generating capacity of 846 MW each.
In congruence with the power market, natural gas prices along the Gulf Coast rose another five to 10 cents today to the $2.60-2.65 per million British thermal units range.
